title: RuptureJobManifest
description: Portable batch-job manifest (ADR-0016). The image and command are what runs; inputs/outputs are DVC paths with remote URIs; the aws block is an annotation a deployer reads and every other platform ignores.

name.description: Job name; equals the file name without .yaml.

status.description: Whether this job has ever been run as written. `run`: the command exists and has been executed at least once, and the core-hour estimate can cite it. `not-run`: the command exists but nothing has executed it here. `command-not-implemented`: the entry point named in `command` does not exist yet, so the manifest is a sized proposal and nothing can run it. A manifest never claims more than this field.

image.description: Image reference. rupture's own image is ${RUPTURE_IMAGE}; the OpenQuake engine is its pinned tag.

command.description: argv run as the container command (the image defines no ENTRYPOINT, only a default CMD). Either the exact `rupture ...` invocation, starting with the token `rupture`, or — for a training entry point that src/rupture/cli.py has not mounted as a verb yet — the module form `python -m rupture.<module> ...` that is runnable today. The module form is a statement that the verb is missing, not a licence to skip it.

core_hours_estimate.description: Expected cost of ONE invocation, in CPU-core-hours: (user + system CPU seconds) / 3600, summed over every core the job uses. This is a cost, not a wall clock and not a ceiling — `cpu` x `timeout_minutes` / 60 is the ceiling, and the estimate must stay at or below it. It is the number a person confirms against before a paid run.

core_hours_basis.description: How the estimate was arrived at. `measured`: this job, as written, was timed and `core_hours_note` cites the log. `extrapolated`: a related run was timed and the note gives the arithmetic that carries it here. `guess`: nothing comparable was timed; the note says so and gives the reasoning. A `guess` is honest; an unlabelled number is not.

core_hours_note.description: The basis in prose: which run was timed, on what host, for which region and placeholder values, and what was assumed to carry it to this job. Long enough to be checkable.

docker_socket.description: True when the command drives a second container (the OpenQuake image) and needs /var/run/docker.sock on the host.

schedule.description: Informational cron (UTC) or null for on-demand jobs. Nothing here triggers anything (docs/SCHEDULER.md describes the scheduler).

env.description: Names of variables the job reads (from .env.example). Never values.
